comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Real-session evidence that this is 'a bridge is genuinely attaching twice' rather than the smoke run racing itself: one run logged nine bridge.start and four bridge.attach.failed, w5:p1 and w5:p4 twice each, and the saved arrangement held four regions for three panes. Two regions on one pane spawn two surfaces, two bridges dial one terminal, and the loser reports this error. Written up in a_2Ht74jTXV - if it is the same bug, fixing the composition fixes this check.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed on the composition side in kan a_2Ht74jTXV, and here is why the check fails inside a run that starts from a deleted scratch directory: every check calling pointed_at(daemon) shares one HOME, so window.toml accumulates across them. 'a bare launch opens a usable window' is the fourth launch in that home and restores what the three before it wrote - a region per launch, each drawing the same pane again. ROOT is deleted once per run, not once per check, which is why a fresh directory did not rule leftover state out.

The fix is two changes in crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs: the standing rule that gives a daemon with nothing on screen a region now waits until the window has opened, and reopen_what_was_left reuses a region already showing a tab rather than opening a second onto it. Covered by three tests in crates/muster-seam/tests/reopen.rs.

Unverified against this check: ./dev --contract launches the real app, and this machine is hosting live agent sessions. Worth re-running the tier before closing this card. The second failing check here, the version-1 fixture, is untouched.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Second half fixed** (`1f56ec1` on main2). It was the fixture, and here is the evidence rather than the inference.

The fixture was added at `99df15f`, when the composition format was at version 1. `284b505` moved it to 2 nine commits later - `region.tab` changed meaning once Muster minted its own tab ids - and nothing connected the two. The app is correct: every `window.toml` written during a contract run says `version = 2`, including the one the app wrote back over this fixture after refusing it.

**The check was worse than red - it was staging nothing.** A refused arrangement is an ignored one, so the window opened as a first launch, and `Presentation::default()` has the sidebar open. The half this check exists to stage - a window remembered with the roster closed - was gone from the day the version moved. It failed on the refusal warning, which is the only reason anybody noticed.

Fixed by reading the version out of `const VERSION` in `crates/muster-core/src/composition/saved.rs` rather than typing it, so the fixture cannot go stale again; a constant that moves or is renamed fails the check with what to do about it. `composition.restore.failed` is deliberately not in the check's `expected` list and a comment says why - declaring it would make a check that stages nothing green.

Verified by running `./dev --contract`: the check passes, and passes for the right reason. No restore failure in the log, and `problems.sidebar.opened` reports "the roster was closed", which is only reachable when the saved arrangement was actually restored.

**First half - not mine, and worth a note.** `a bare launch opens a usable window` is intermittent at `4eb15a3`, which is before slot 1's fix lands. Three runs of the tier this evening: pass, fail, pass. The card's original account has it reproducing twice in a row, so whatever slot 1 fixed, the symptom here is a race rather than a certainty - worth knowing when confirming the fix, since one green run will not settle it.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Re-ran `./dev --contract` on integrated main (87427ee, all three shakedown slots landed). **The first half of this card is confirmed fixed.**

    ok    a named pane comes up and paints
      ok    the app as it ships paints every pane
      ok    an agent's state reaches the window
      ok    a pane that does not exist says why
      ok    a bare launch opens a usable window        <- was FAIL
      ok    a clean machine gets a daemon and a workspace
      ok    a pane can drive the window it is drawn in
      FAIL  a refused config opens the roster it would have had nowhere to appear in
      ok    a split tab becomes splits, all of them typeable

So the composition-side fix in a_2Ht74jTXV does clear this check, which the comment above could not verify at the time. Seven of eight now pass.

The second half is unchanged - four copies of `composition.restore.failed`, the version-1 fixture against a Muster that writes version 2. Being worked now; the card stays open until that lands.

One thing this run also settles: the tier is runnable while a real Muster session is live on the same machine. `tools/smoke-launch.py` gives the app a scratch HOME and its own XDG dirs, so it never meets the user's daemon or state files. The earlier caution about needing a quiet machine applies to --perf, not to this.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Both halves fixed, and the tier is green end to end on integrated main (4638494):

    ok  a named pane comes up and paints
      ok  the app as it ships paints every pane
      ok  an agent's state reaches the window
      ok  a pane that does not exist says why
      ok  a bare launch opens a usable window
      ok  a clean machine gets a daemon and a workspace
      ok  a pane can drive the window it is drawn in
      ok  a refused config opens the roster it would have had nowhere to appear in
      ok  a split tab becomes splits, all of them typeable
    exit 0

The first half went with the composition fix in a_2Ht74jTXV. The second turned out to be worse than a stale fixture: the check had been asserting nothing since 2026-08-17, because a version-1 window.toml was refused, the window opened as a first launch, and a first launch's roster is open - which is the state the check was staging its way out of. It failed on the refusal, which is the only reason anybody noticed. The version is now read out of const VERSION rather than typed, so the next move fails the check with what to do about it.

Closing.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`./dev --contract` has two checks failing on a clean scratch directory at HEAD, unrelated to whatever change you are running it for. A tier that is red before you start is one nobody can judge anything with, which is worse than not having it - found while verifying kan a_29i4bxafd, where establishing that these predate the change cost a stash and a second full build.

**`a bare launch opens a usable window`** fails on an error the app itself logs:

    bridge.attach.failed - terminal attach failed: terminal term_... already
    has an attached client; retry with --takeover
    impact: this window stays empty for as long as it is open

Reproduced twice on a freshly deleted `/private/tmp/muster-smoke`, so it is not leftover state. Whether the smoke run is racing itself or a bridge is genuinely attaching twice is the thing to find out.

**`a refused config opens the roster it would have had nowhere to appear in`** fails on four copies of one warning:

    composition.restore.failed - the saved arrangement is version 1 and this
    Muster writes version 2

The fixture writes a `window.toml` the app no longer reads. That looks like a fixture left behind when the composition format moved to version 2, in which case the fix is the fixture rather than the app - worth confirming rather than assuming, since the same warning would appear if the app had stopped writing version 2.

Both confirmed present at HEAD with the working tree stashed, so neither comes from the daemon-launch work.
title: 🚨 Two contract checks fail at HEAD, so the tier says nothing
